title: Infinity vs Stripe: Best for Global Payments in India?
summary: Infinity vs Stripe for Indian businesses: Compare international payment fees, FX rates, settlement times, features and benefits to find the right fit.
body_markdown:
## Infinity vs Stripe: Head-to-Head


This section compares both on the five points that matter most to an Indian business: how you get paid, fees, speed, compliance and support.


### 1. How you get paid


**Stripe collects card payments, and Infinity collects bank transfers.** That is the biggest difference, and it decides who each one suits.


With Stripe, your customer enters card details and pays. This works well for online shops, subscriptions and quick purchases. With Infinity, your client sends money from their bank to the account details you share. This works well for invoices, retainers, project payments and export receipts.


Many businesses see both types of payments, which is why some use both tools.


### 2. Fees and pricing structure


**Stripe's fee depends on the card type, and a currency conversion fee and GST are added on top. Infinity charges a flat 0.5% that includes everything.**


Here is Stripe's fee structure for India as published:

If a currency conversion is required on a transaction, Stripe adds a 2% fee. GST is charged on Stripe's fees.


To see how that stacks up, take a customer paying with a Visa or Mastercard issued outside India. The card fee is 3%. If the payment needs currency conversion, add 2%. That is 5% before GST. For other international cards, the base fee is 4.3%, and with conversion it is 6.3% before GST.


Infinity's fee is 0.5% all-inclusive, with no separate FX markup and no extra GST.

### 3. Settlement speed


**Infinity settles in 24 hours. Stripe settles your payments in 3-4 days to your Indian bank account in INR.**


For a business that runs on tight cash flow, the gap matters. Waiting several days for card payouts is workable for steady online sales, but it can feel slow when you are waiting on a large client invoice to pay salaries or vendors.


### 4. FIRA, purpose codes and RBI compliance


**Infinity generates a free FIRA automatically. Stripe does not give an automatic FIRA, but it sends a payment advice that you can use to request a FIRC from your bank.**


Here is what each term means in simple words:


-


**FIRA (Foreign Inward Remittance Advice):** a document that proves you received money from abroad.


-


**FIRC (Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate):** a similar certificate issued by your bank.


-


**Purpose code:** an RBI code that tells the bank why the money was sent, such as software services.


On Stripe, Indian users get a payment advice from Standard Chartered Bank by email on the day the export payout is processed. You take this advice to your bank to obtain a FIRC. So the paperwork is possible, but it is a manual step.


Stripe also lets an account carry only one transaction purpose code. It evaluates the code you pick against your business, and says it cannot advise you on the right code. If you offer more than one kind of service, that single code can become a limit.


On Infinity, the FIRA is generated automatically and is free. Infinity also has a purpose code finder tool, which helps you pick the correct purpose code for your payment.


Why does this matter? Exporters often need proof of receipt for GST refunds, export incentives and records. Having it ready without chasing the bank saves time.


### 5. Support and onboarding


**Infinity gives you a dedicated personal account manager. Stripe's help runs mainly through its dashboard and email.**


On onboarding, Infinity takes about 2 minutes to sign up, with KYC completed the same day. Stripe requires an invite first, then identification details, a website or app link, a business description and bank details.


## When Does Stripe Make More Sense, and When Does Infinity?


**This decision is based on how your customers pay you:**


### 1.Stripe may fit better if:


-


You run a website or app where customers pay by card at checkout.


-


You sell subscriptions and need built-in recurring billing.


-


You are a registered company, LLP or sole proprietorship and have secured an invite.


-


Your developers want to build a custom checkout.


### 2. Infinity may fit better if:


-


You bill clients abroad by invoice, and they pay by bank transfer.


-


You are a freelancer, agency, exporter or startup founder who wants simple sign-up without waiting for an invite.


-


You want a flat 0.5% all-inclusive fee with no separate FX markup or GST.


-


You want a free FIRA without manual follow-ups.


-


You want settlement in 24 hours.


### 3. Can you use both?


Yes. A SaaS company might use Stripe for card subscriptions from customers and Infinity for larger client contracts paid by bank transfer. The two do not compete for the same payment flow.


If you are comparing more options, see our guide to the[best alternatives to Stripe for global payments in India](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/the-best-alternatives-to-stripe-for-global-payments-in-india) . If PayPal is also on your list, read our[Stripe vs PayPal comparison](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/stripe-vs-paypal) .


## How to get started with Stripe in India


Follow the following ways to get started with Stripe in India:


1.


Request an invite through Stripe's sales contact form.


2.


Keep your business registration details, identification numbers, website or app link and bank details ready.


3.


Get your IEC if you export goods, or if you want to accept American Express payments.


4.


Select your transaction purpose code during onboarding.


5.


Complete KYC and integrate checkout, passing the customer details Stripe needs for export reporting.


## How to get started with Infinity


Follow the following ways to get started with Infinity in India:


1.


Sign up on the Infinity website or mobile app in about 2 minutes.


2.


Complete verification and KYC, which is done the same day.


3.


Receive bank details in multiple currencies.


4.


Share the details with your client and start receiving payments.

## How Does Infinity Help Receive International Payments?


Infinity is built for Indian businesses that get paid from abroad. It supports 50+ currencies and 160+ countries, and it charges 0.5% all-inclusive with no additional GST. Settlement takes 24 hours, and a free FIRA is generated automatically. You also get a dedicated personal account manager and a dedicated mobile app to track your payments.


It is RBI-regulated and AD-1 certified, and more than 10,000 users have already onboarded. If you want to start receiving international payments without waiting for an invite, you can sign up with Infinity in about 2 minutes.


## Conclusion


Stripe and Infinity are different tools for different jobs. Stripe is a strong card checkout tool, but it is currently invite-only in India, charges fees that depend on card type plus conversion and GST, and does not give an automatic FIRA. Infinity is built to receive international payments by bank transfer, with simple sign-up, a flat 0.5% all-inclusive fee, 24-hour settlement and a free FIRA.


If your business bills clients abroad, Infinity is likely the better fit. If you need card checkout and can get an invite, Stripe is worth considering, and some businesses will use both.


## FAQs on Stripe vs Infinity for International Payments


### Infinity vs Stripe: Which Fits Indian Businesses Better for Global Payments?


Infinity fits better if you receive client payments and invoices from abroad by bank transfer. Stripe fits better if you need card checkout on a website or app and have an invite. They are built for different payment flows, so some businesses use both.


### Is Stripe available in India?


Yes, but only by invite. Indian businesses cannot sign up for a new Stripe account on the website and must request an invite from Stripe.


### Is Stripe invite-only in India?


Yes. Stripe moved to invite-only in India in May 2024. Active accounts continue to work, and new businesses need to request an invite.


### How much does Stripe charge in India for international payments?


Stripe charges 3% for Visa or Mastercard issued outside India, 3.5% for American Express and 4.3% for other international cards. A 2% fee is added when currency conversion is needed, and GST is charged on top.


### Does Stripe charge GST in India?


Yes. GST is charged on Stripe's fees in India. Infinity charges no additional GST on its 0.5% all-inclusive fee.


### Does Stripe give an automatic FIRA?


No. Stripe does not generate a FIRA automatically. It sends a payment advice from Standard Chartered Bank, which you can take to your bank to request a FIRC. Infinity generates a free FIRA automatically.


### Does Stripe India need an IEC?


For goods exports, yes. For services, an IEC is optional, but you still need one to accept American Express payments from international customers.


### Can freelancers use Stripe in India?


Only if they are registered as a company, LLP or sole proprietorship. Individuals cannot accept international payments on Stripe in India, and new accounts are invite-only.


### How do I get a Stripe account in India?


Request an invite through Stripe's sales contact form, then share your business details, identification numbers, a website or app link and bank details for review.


### Is Infinity cheaper than Stripe?


For international payments, Infinity's 0.5% all-inclusive fee is lower than Stripe's 3% to 4.3% card fee plus a 2% conversion fee and GST. The right choice still depends on how your customers pay you.


### Can I use Infinity and Stripe together?


Yes. Many businesses use Stripe for card checkout and Infinity for client payments received by bank transfer.
